---
title: "The parser layer"
---

Every ESPN wrapper can return either the **raw JSON `Dict`** ESPN ships or a
**tidy DataFrame** produced by the parser layer. This guide shows both, side by
side, executed at build time.

## `return_parsed` — raw `Dict` vs tidy frame

For parser-backed ESPN wrappers, `return_parsed=True` is the **default**, so you
get a polars frame out of the box. Pass `return_parsed=False` to recover the raw
payload.

```{python}
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_team_roster

raw = espn_nba_team_roster(team_id=13, return_parsed=False)   # -> Dict
print("raw payload type:", type(raw).__name__)
print("top-level keys:", list(raw.keys())[:10])
```

The same call with the default `return_parsed=True` gives a tidy frame:

```{python}
df = espn_nba_team_roster(team_id=13)   # -> polars.DataFrame (default)
print("parsed frame:", df.shape)
df.columns[:16]
```

## `return_as_pandas` — one frame, two engines

The package is polars-first but pandas-friendly. Because the cache key excludes
`return_as_pandas`, a single stored frame serves both callers — the conversion
happens on read.

```{python}
from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_teams

pl_frame = espn_nba_teams()                       # polars
pd_frame = espn_nba_teams(return_as_pandas=True)  # pandas

print("polars type:", type(pl_frame).__name__)
print("pandas type:", type(pd_frame).__name__)
print("same row count:", pl_frame.height == len(pd_frame))
```

Quarto renders the pandas frame just as happily (note the `df-print: paged`
styling from `_quarto.yml`):

```{python}
pd_frame[["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_display_name"]].head(5)
```

## Sibling-API parsers compose explicitly

NHL and MLB have their own native APIs whose wrappers return raw `Dict` and pair
with a named parser you apply yourself. The shape is
`parse_<x>(<wrapper>(...))`:

```python
from sportsdataverse.nhl import nhl_web_pbp, parse_nhl_web_pbp

df = parse_nhl_web_pbp(nhl_web_pbp(2023030417))   # 331-row polars frame
```

::: {.callout-note}
The parser contract is universal: empty/malformed payloads return a **zero-row
frame** (not an exception), so you can chain without null-checks, and columns are
snake-cased. See [Architecture](../architecture.qmd) for the full picture.
:::
